summary: Two tests (line 3025, 3101) drive real x-key press through the Textual pilot against the real WorkflowsScreen/DeleteWorkflowScreen; one moves the cursor via 'down' before pressing x (targets 'second'), the other presses x on the default highlight (targets 'first' and asserts 'second' is absent) — genuinely distinguishing highlighted-row targeting, and both assert the screen swaps to a real confirmation dialog with Yes/No buttons and message text. Only the REST client is faked; the key binding, cursor-based row selection, and modal-opening logic run unmocked.
